newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-HINGIS, GRAF STILL ON COURSE FOR FINAL SHOWDOWN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS, GRAF STILL ON COURSE FOR FINAL SHOWDOWN.

text.p: The dream women's final between Martina Hingis and Steffi Graf, which looked an unlikely prospect when the French Open started, may take place after all.
Five times champion Graf and the teenager who ousted her from the top spot in the world rankings last March must still clear some tricky hurdles if they want to face each other next Sunday.
But they have both used their early matches to boost their confidence, reaching the quarter-finals more smoothly than expected after battling recent injuries.
"Coming here, I didn't think I would compete as well as I have so far," said top seed Hingis, playing her first tournament since hurting her knee in a horse riding accident last month.
The 16-year-old Hingis, who beat Austria's Barbara Paulus 6-3 0-6 6-0 in a strange match to advance to the last eight on Sunday, now faces a tough test against Spain's Arantxa Sanchez Vicario.
"I feel very confident," said Sanchez Vicario, disappointing so far this season but always a threat when it comes to the French Open, which she won in 1989 and 1994.
"This tournament is very special to me and I'm feeling better every day," she added. "I feel confident. All the pressure will be on Martina."

Graf, still wearing a bandage on the injured left knee which sidelined her for three months earlier in the season, looked as fit as ever on her way to her 6-7 6-2 6-2 win over Romania's Irina Spirlea.
"It was good to play a match under difficult conditions and to fight it out," said Graf. "I'm slowly finding my rhythm...I haven't been feeling that well for weeks."
Second seed Graf, who will appear in the quarter-finals at Roland Garros for the 12th consecutive year, next meets an opponent she knows well in Amanda Coetzer.

The diminutive South African, who impressed by overcoming Spain's Conchita Martinez for the first time on Sunday, has beaten Graf twice this season, including an embarrassing 6-0 6-1 victory at the German Open.
American Monica Seles, who has attracted little attention, nevertheless made it to the quarter-finals of an event she won three times in a row from 1990 to 1992.
Yugoslav-born Seles, seeded third this year, shrugged off a brave challenge from local favourite Mary Pierce of France to win an exciting match 6-4 7-5 on Sunday.
"I knew I had to be focused, playing Mary as well as the crowd," she said. "Today, I was pretty close to having everything working well."
Seles next meets 12th seed Mary Joe Fernandez, who struggled before moving past fellow American Lisa Raymond 6-7 6-2 6-2.
"I haven't played Mary Joe for a long time and she's playing good tennis at the moment so it will be tough," said Seles. "I'm not thinking about the title, I'm only worrying about my next match."

Croat Iva Majoli, the ninth seed, upset fifth seed American Lindsay Davenport in three sets to set up an intriguing showdown with Romania's Ruxandra Dragomir, the only non-seeded player left in the women's draw.
Quarter-final line up:
1-Martina Hingis (Switzerland) v 6-Arantxa Sanchez Vicario (Spain)
3-Monica Seles (U.S.) v 12-Mary Joe Fernandez (U.S.)
9-Iva Majoli (Croatia) v Ruxandra Dragomir (Romania)
11-Amanda Coetzer (South Africa) v 2-Steffi Graf (Germany).
